name: Procreate
summary: The iPad painting app most digital illustrators start with.
gap: Brush feel and Apple Pencil latency are the entire product. A clone that misses those is a drawing app nobody opens twice.

name: Adobe Photoshop
summary: The raster editor that the word 'photoshopped' comes from.
gap: Nobody wants another layer stack. They want the dozen features they actually open Photoshop for, without the weight or the subscription.

name: Adobe Illustrator
summary: Vector drawing and logo work, and the pen tool people love to hate.
gap: Bezier editing is muscle memory for a generation. Matching the pen tool, then making it kinder, is the whole job.

name: Adobe Lightroom
summary: Batch photo editing and cataloguing for photographers.
gap: The catalogue matters as much as the sliders. Import, cull, sync and export. Get those four fast and the rest follows.

name: Figma
summary: Browser-based interface design and the multiplayer canvas that ate the category.
gap: Multiplayer cursors are the easy part. A clone lives or dies on vector performance and a plugin surface other people can extend.

name: Canva
summary: Drag-and-drop design for people who are not designers.
gap: The templates are the product. A nicer editor with no library of starting points has nothing to sell.

name: Miro
summary: Infinite whiteboards for workshops and diagramming.
gap: Infinite canvas, sticky notes and a facilitator mode. Anything slower than a real corkboard loses the room.

name: Anima
summary: Design-to-code handoff: turn frames into front-end markup.
gap: The generated markup has to be something a developer keeps. Anything that gets thrown away after review is a toy.

name: Squarespace
summary: Template-driven sites for people who want to look professional quickly.
gap: Taste in the defaults. The value is the template, the type pairing, and the fact that nothing needs configuring.

name: Webflow
summary: Visual building that exports real, production HTML and CSS.
gap: The output has to be clean enough that a developer accepts it. Visual builders die on markup people are embarrassed to ship.

name: Adobe Premiere Pro
summary: The default timeline editor for video that ships on a deadline.
gap: Timeline responsiveness on real footage is the bar. Proxy workflows and codec support matter more than a prettier UI.

name: Logic Pro
summary: Apple's full studio: recording, MIDI, mixing and mastering.
gap: You cannot fake a sampler or a mixing bus. A clone needs one workflow done deeply (tracking, or beatmaking), not a bit of everything.

name: Blender
summary: Free 3D modelling, animation, rendering and compositing.
gap: Blender is already free, so a clone has to win on approachability: a modelling tool a beginner can finish something in.

name: Notion
summary: Docs, databases and wikis in one workspace.
gap: Flexible blocks are easy; a database engine that does not stutter at ten thousand rows is not. Speed is the differentiator.

name: Obsidian
summary: Local-first markdown notes with backlinks and a plugin ecosystem.
gap: Plain files on disk are the selling point. Any clone that puts your notes in someone else's database has lost the argument.

name: Evernote
summary: The notebook app that defined web clipping.
gap: Clipping and search across years of notes. A clone that cannot import an existing archive is a notebook nobody can move into.

name: Todoist
summary: Fast, keyboard-driven task capture and projects.
gap: Capture speed and a natural-language parser. If adding a task takes longer than typing it into a text file, it is already dead.

name: Google Sheets
summary: The spreadsheet everyone actually collaborates in.
gap: Formulas plus sharing, with real-time presence that does not fight you. Most clones underestimate the formula surface.

name: Microsoft Excel
summary: The spreadsheet that runs a surprising amount of the world.
gap: Pivot tables and keyboard shortcuts. Nobody leaves Excel for a nicer grid; they leave for something that does one hard thing well.

name: Google Calendar
summary: The calendar most people's week actually lives in.
gap: Reading and writing somebody else's calendar reliably is the hard part. The scheduling logic is the product.

name: 1Password
summary: Password manager with a serious security reputation.
gap: Crypto is the easiest part to get right and the easiest to get catastrophically wrong. No credible security story means it is a liability.

name: Zoom
summary: Video meetings, and the verb for them.
gap: Call quality on a bad connection. The grid, the chat and the reactions are decoration on top of reliable audio.

name: Slack
summary: Channel-based chat for teams.
gap: A clone has to be somewhere people already are, or replace email outright. Notification discipline is the real feature.

name: Jira
summary: Issue tracking and sprint planning for software teams.
gap: Jira's weakness is its own flexibility. A clone that picks one workflow and refuses to be configured is a genuine improvement.

name: Toggl Track
summary: One-button time tracking and the reports that come out of it.
gap: Starting a timer has to cost nothing. Every clone that asks you to categorise first has already lost the day.

name: Vercel
summary: Hosting and preview deployments for front-end teams.
gap: A preview per branch and a deploy that is boring. Git integration and cold-start speed are the whole pitch.

name: Sentry
summary: Error and performance monitoring for shipped apps.
gap: Grouping errors sensibly is the hard part. A clone with noisy alerts or fake-looking stack traces makes things worse.

name: Discourse
summary: Self-hosted forum software for communities that outlive a chat app.
gap: Threading, moderation and search that survives a decade of posts. Moderation tools are the unglamorous core.

name: WordPress
summary: The CMS behind a large share of the web, themes and plugins included.
gap: Plugins are the moat and the mess. A clone that ships the twenty plugins everyone installs, pre-wired, is immediately useful.

name: Shopify
summary: Hosted storefronts: catalogue, checkout, payments and shipping.
gap: Checkout, tax and payments. A pretty storefront is easy; being the merchant of record is not.

name: QuickBooks
summary: Bookkeeping for small businesses and the accountants who file for them.
gap: Accountants have to accept the output. A clone that cannot export a standard ledger format is a hobby project.

name: YNAB
summary: Envelope-method budgeting that people stay loyal to for years.
gap: It is a method, not a UI. A clone that copies the screens and drops the philosophy has nothing left.

name: MyFitnessPal
summary: Calorie and macro tracking with a giant food database.
gap: The food database is the product. Logging has to take seconds or nobody keeps it up past week two.

name: Habitica
summary: Habit tracking turned into a role-playing game.
gap: Habit apps live or die on the reminder and the streak. The game layer is optional; the nudge is not.

name: Duolingo
summary: Bite-sized language lessons with a notoriously sticky streak.
gap: The curriculum and the guilt. Streak mechanics are easy to copy and hard to make kind.

name: Anki
summary: Spaced repetition for people studying something genuinely hard.
gap: The scheduling algorithm and syncing between devices. Prettier decks do not make anyone remember more.

name: Spotify
summary: Streaming music, playlists and the recommendations that made it huge.
gap: Licensing, which is exactly why nobody vibecodes a Spotify. A clone that plays your own files and recommends differently is realistic.

name: Winamp
summary: The music player people kept open purely for the visualiser.
gap: Nostalgia plus audio reactivity. It is a toy, so it only has to be fun once, which is a low bar and a high bar at the same time.

name: Wordle
summary: One word puzzle a day, and the group chat it spawned.
gap: The daily constraint is the whole design. A clone with infinite puzzles and no shared reset loses the ritual.

name: Google Photos
summary: Photo backup, search and sharing across every device you own.
gap: Search that works without you tagging anything. Local-first storage is the obvious differentiator.

name: WeTransfer
summary: Send big files without anyone making an account.
gap: Three clicks and a link. Anything that asks you to sign up has already lost to the thing it is replacing.

name: Dropbox
summary: File sync that just works, on every machine you own.
gap: Conflict-free sync is genuinely hard. A clone that silently loses one file is worse than no clone at all.

name: Mailchimp
summary: Email lists, campaigns and the automations that drip out of them.
gap: Deliverability. A clone sending from a random IP lands in spam. The unsexy infrastructure is the product.

name: Buffer
summary: Plan and publish social posts across several networks.
gap: The rules change constantly and API access is the moat. A clone that handles one network properly beats a broken five.

name: Beamer
summary: In-app changelogs and announcements, with reactions from users.
gap: It has to sit inside the product, not next to it. A clone that is just a blog with a date field is a blog.

name: Google Analytics
summary: Web traffic analytics, and the consent banner that comes with them.
gap: Cookie-free, privacy-respecting stats that load in two kilobytes. The backlash is the opportunity.

name: Linear
summary: The keyboard-driven issue tracker beloved by modern software teams.
gap: The shortcuts and 60fps keyboard navigation are the product. A clone with laggy modals or mouse-first menus is just a slow issue tracker.

name: Calendly
summary: One-click meeting scheduling links that eliminate email back-and-forth.
gap: Time zone math and bi-directional calendar conflict resolution. If two people can book the same slot, the tool is a liability.

name: Trello
summary: Visual drag-and-drop Kanban boards for organizing anything.
gap: Frictionless card dragging and multi-user sync. If moving a card stutters or drops mid-drag, the visual metaphor falls apart.

name: Loom
summary: Quick screen and webcam video recording with instant shareable links.
gap: Instant encoding and zero-wait uploading. If the creator has to wait 3 minutes for video processing after hitting stop, the moment is gone.

name: Perplexity
summary: Conversational answer engine with real-time web search and citation cards.
gap: Live citation grounding and streaming latency. A search clone that hallucinates dead links or takes ten seconds to start streaming loses the user.
